items.label: Industry: GLP-1 / Metabolic & Obesity Therapeutics
items.detail: Selected from active-conviction account holdings: LLY (Eli Lilly, 10 sh, $11,575, 2.36% of NAV) is the account's sole Healthcare position and has pulled back roughly 5-9% from its July 2026 all-time high on a mix of profit-taking, GLP-1 pricing pressure, and competitive/legal crosscurrents -- worth a full thesis check rather than assuming the pullback is noise. This theme is distinct from the account's two most recent scout cycles (AI Datacenter Power Infrastructure on 2026-08-30, Critical Minerals & Precious Metals Mining on 2026-08-31 earlier today), avoiding repeat coverage.

items.label: LLY
items.detail: Existing holding, thesis reinforced with real new evidence, but with genuine new headwinds: Lilly's oral pill Foundayo (orforglipron), launched April 2026, is projected to reach $19B in sales by 2035 (15% of total revenue) and command roughly 60% ($13.6B) of the 2030 daily-oral GLP-1 segment versus Novo's 21% ($4B) -- but Q2 2026 results showed realized US price on Zepbound/Mounjaro down ~9% amid intensifying competition, PepsiCo and other large employers dropping GLP-1 coverage, and Novo Nordisk's federal lawsuit alleging false comparative advertising. Lilly and Novo together still control ~87% of prescription weight-management revenue.
items.diversification_note: Already the account's entire Healthcare sector bucket (2.36% of NAV, $11,575, sole holding) -- reinforcing here deepens an existing single-stock sector bet rather than diversifying it.

items.label: VKTX
items.detail: Viking Therapeutics -- not currently held. VK2735, a dual GLP-1/GIP agonist advancing in both injectable and oral formulations simultaneously, carries a widely cited 38.5% Polymarket-implied probability of being acquired before 2027; Pfizer (having appointed Morgan Stanley as an advisor per reports), Merck, and Amgen are named as potential suitors in the post-Vertex/Crinetics ($10B) M&A wave repricing third-tier obesity assets. Last price $32.42.
items.diversification_note: Would land in the account's Healthcare bucket alongside LLY (2.36% of NAV) -- a second name in the same sector, but a structurally different bet (pre-revenue M&A-target biotech vs. Lilly's cash-generating franchise).
items.suggested_size: Starter/scout position, roughly 0.5-1% of account NAV (~$2,500-$5,000); binary M&A-speculation risk means the position should be sized assuming the takeout never happens.

items.label: GPCR
items.detail: Structure Therapeutics -- not currently held. Its oral small-molecule GLP-1 candidate aleniglipron posted 16.3% placebo-adjusted weight loss at 44 weeks in Phase 2, with a pivotal Phase 3 study slated to start in H2 2026; multiple sources note Structure would inherit the scarcity premium in obesity-biotech M&A if Viking is taken out first. Last price $45.86.
items.diversification_note: Would also land in the account's Healthcare bucket alongside LLY and VKTX -- differentiated within the sleeve by an all-oral (not injectable) delivery platform, but does not diversify outside the sector.
items.suggested_size: Smallest scout tranche of the group, roughly 0.25-0.5% of account NAV (~$1,250-$2,500); one Phase 3 program away from a binary readout, no approved product yet.

items.label: AMGN
items.detail: Amgen -- not currently held. MariTide (maridebart cafraglutide), a peptide-antibody conjugate combining GIP blockade with GLP-1 activation, showed up to ~20% weight loss with no plateau at 52 weeks in Phase 2 and enables monthly (not weekly) dosing -- a real differentiator on the adherence problem that limits weekly injectables. Phase 3 MARITIME data across obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, and sleep apnea are expected through 2027, so there is no near-term catalyst; flagging the dosing-frequency angle for the next scout cycle rather than a specific action now. Last price $431.01.

items.label: NVO
items.detail: Novo Nordisk -- not currently held. The other half of the GLP-1 duopoly is trading near multi-year lows (ADR last $45.53, down sharply from 2024/2025 highs) after CagriSema trial disappointments and share loss to Lilly's oral pill; its own oral semaglutide is still projected to hold a real (if smaller, ~$4B) share of the 2030 oral segment, and it is the plaintiff, not the defendant, in the current advertising litigation with Lilly. A contrarian value angle on the same duopoly LLY sits in, but continued share-loss momentum is a real near-term risk worth watching before sizing a position.

items.label: FDA compounding crackdown & indication expansion
items.detail: Two structural theme-level signals, no specific ticker yet: (1) the FDA's April 2026 proposal to permanently exclude semaglutide/tirzepatide/liraglutide from the 503B Bulks List, plus 55+ warning letters issued to telehealth compounders in March and June 2026, is closing the generic-copy substitute channel and should structurally redirect volume back to branded drugs (LLY, NVO) over 2026-2027; (2) indication expansion into MASH/NASH, obstructive sleep apnea, and cardiovascular disease (already in Amgen's and others' pipelines) could expand the addressable market well beyond the $27.5B-$68.65B 2026 weight-loss-market estimates currently being modeled -- carry both to the next scout cycle for name-level follow-up.
